variant.title: Known · kit · the Sevan kit only, physical light
variant.summary: known-full's hang with ONLY what ran at Sevan (owner 2026-10-09): all 50 UP-PL5403, all 18 UP-B380F, the 6 LaserCube Ultra MK2 (6 W, drawn as laser lines: 4 mm, 1 mrad, flux per colour from W x V(lambda)) and ONE UP-YZ31P smoke machine as the only haze source — no hazers. The haze is not calibrated to photographs (calibrate: false): it is the two-zone estimate (Nicas 1996) for one Antari Z-1500 III-equivalent in the hall's 186,890 m3, UNVALIDATED. A copy beside known-full; known-full is unchanged.

provenance.optics: From the fixtures manifest (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json): each class names a fixture kind whose beam angle and output come from the maker's published page or, where the maker publishes none, a named equivalent — every number carries its source there. The rental house's own datasheets are still OWED to confirm.
provenance.positions: Placed by rule against the hall's structural grid (scripts/place/hall.py -> hall.json), so they move when the hall is rebuilt with measured dimensions.
provenance.hall: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-28.json (flat space-frame roof, 4 spans x 24 m, 18 bays; photos + 2020 satellite) + moxir-hall-features-2026-09-28.json (the owner's zones marked 2026-09-28, the press massing, gates, cranes; sizes estimated).
provenance.models: Fixture bodies are the models in scripts/place/fixtures/glb, built to the datasheet dimensions by scripts/place/fixtures/build_fixtures.py (see the manifest for provenance and licence).
provenance.stage: The owner, 2026-09-28, on the first rebuild: "i mention the dj place i think it will not big how you created you made it so big, so stage is the near the metal thing like dj near a bit top and centre of the metal things". So the 'stage' is a DJ place: a small riser, a bit raised, centred on the forging press ('the metal things'), close in front of it; the machinery is the picture behind the DJ. Positions from the photographs (photo 032's fitted camera, cross-checked from photo 004 with EXIF intrinsics; scripts/place/photo_meta.py).
provenance.versions: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-versions-2026-10-17.json: 2026-09-28, on /moxir: "make 3 version with the full, midle, and simple minimalistic and also look to moxir mood, set, vibe and its the undegroudn rave thing lights like that not the commercial shit"

assumptions: The DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28) is a riser of stage decks 3 m wide x 2 m deep x 1.2 m high ON THE NAVE CENTRE LINE (x 0; the owner, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'), its back edge 1.0 m in front of the press's face (z 3.2 m, +-1.5 m), facing the entry and the crowd. The press stays where it stands, 1.65 m right of the axis (range 0.5-3.5), behind the right half of the riser. Three 2 x 1 m decks on 1.2 m legs; 'a bit top' read as 1.0-1.4 m. Options considered: stage.options (D chosen).

The DJ stands behind a 1.8 x 0.8 m DJ table, 0.95 m high, at the riser's front edge; treads up the left side (toward the backstage); a crowd barrier 1.3 m in front of the riser, 9 m long. The crowd (blue) fills the floor from the barrier to under the crane.

The machinery stays the backdrop: the press (to 5.3 m) stands behind the right half of the riser and the machine line beside it further right, so from the floor the DJ is seen against the press; the goalpost header at 7 m is above the press's crown.

No stage deck, no towers: the DJ stand alone. THE CUT: one straight 12 m line of 290 mm square box truss, planned on the Prolyte H30V (4 × H30V-L300; the rental house's own truss and its load table owed), sloped 15° in the bridge's plane — bottom chord 3.24 m at house left (x -6.04) to 6.35 m at house right (x 5.55) — on 3 bridled chain hoists at their shortest drop, with safety steels and a tie-off at each end; load on the line ≈ 250 kg, 44 / 146 / 59 kg a pick (house left → right, ESTIMATE). rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

Lasers stand on the top plates of the two towers (7.15 m) and are aimed UP into the roof over the audience; the rig script refuses any laser aim that descends, and any that passes under 3 m above the floor. This is a picture of intent, not a laser safety assessment — a qualified laser safety officer and the national rules (e.g. the Maximum Permissible Exposure limits of IEC 60825-1) are OWED before any 40 W laser is switched on in front of people.

Strobes, blinders and hazers are other-supplier lines (the rental house lists none): each is a planning type modelled on a named product (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json, EXT- codes). No CO2 jet, cold spark or confetti — the underground brief (versions file, method).

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Every lamp but the press's own six mirrors about the nave centre line (x 0), the booth's axis too. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

stage.label: DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28)
stage.intent: owner's words 2026-09-28: 'dj place ... not big ... near the metal thing ... a bit top and centre of the metal things'
stage.decks: 3 x stage deck 2 x 1 m (e.g. Bütec / Nivtec / Litedeck class) on 1.2 m legs

centre_x_m.how: the nave axis, by the owner's choice; the press behind it is at x 1.65 (range 0.5-3.5), so the riser (x -1.5..1.5) overlaps the press's face from x 0.25 to 1.5

press_face_z_m.how: photo 032: D 47 m from the crane camera; photo 004: base at D 43 m from a camera at z 47 -> z 3.7

options.why: centred on the press, the tallest of the metal things and the one he drew along (1c3956d1); the machine line reads beside it to the right — chosen first (01:00-04:00), the owner found the scene off-centre
the smallest booth: 2 decks, room for a DJ and a table only; no space for a second DJ or the booth-top beams
centred on the press AND the rusty machine line beside it (x 0.25..8): the visual middle of 'the metal things' seen from the floor, but the riser would stand in the machinery on the SW half

on the hall's axis, so the whole rig and the room's first screen mirror about one line (the owner's call, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'); the press stands 1.65 m right of centre behind the DJ, still overlapping the riser

stage.centred: on the NAVE centre line (x 0), owner 2026-09-28 04:13: 'make the scene in center it not the center right?' — option D. The press stays where it stands (x 0.25..3.05, centre 1.65), 1.65 m right of the booth's axis behind it.

truss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss, planned on the Prolyte H30V (4 × H30V-L300; the rental house's own truss and its load table owed)
truss.slope_why: the steepest slope the brief's two ends allow together: the high end is capped by the bridle at the high pick (below), the low end kept ≈ 3.5 m; 15° is the brief's floor for reading as a deliberate slash, not a sag
truss.x_offset_why: the line runs u −6.25…+5.75 along itself (x −6.04…+5.55): a clamp point every 0.5 m, 0.25 m in from each end (src/rigbuild/pieces.js), then falls on the DJ's axis, so every lamp stands on a clamp point and the centre beam sits over the DJ
truss.trim_at: trim_m (derived) is the bottom chord at u = 0, over the DJ's axis, measured vertically; the high pick sets it (versions.mjs craneCut)
truss.why: The owner's pick, 2026-09-29: option 4 of ~/Downloads/moxir-crane-rig/ten-truss.html (also https://dev.diiii.xyz/moxir/p/moxir-truss) — 'the cut': ONE straight 12 m truss in the vertical plane right under the yellow crane bridge, LOW house left (−x), HIGH house right (+x, over the forging press and the machine line). Chosen for being epic AND easy: a plain straight truss, 3 hanging points, nothing on the floor. It replaces Minimal's 8 m flat line (x −4.25…3.75, bottom chord 6.0 m, 2 hoists).
truss.trim_why: derived (versions.mjs craneCut): the high pick's bridle at its 120° limit puts its apex at 7.37 m; the hoist's shortest drop under it (0.85 m) and the chords at that pick leave 4.86 m for the bottom chord over the axis

rigging.picks_why: 3 picks: 0.5 m in from each end and one near the middle (u −0.5: between the centre beam and its neighbour, so no beam rises through a bridle or a chain); spans 5.25 and 5.75 m — well inside the H30V's table (Prolyte: 6 m span, uniformly distributed 321.6 kg/m allowable)
rigging.hoist: chain hoist 500 kg, D8 Plus (planned on the CHAINMASTER D8Plus Ultra 500 kg SK030/76U; the rental house's hoists owed)
rigging.hoist_kg_source: CHAINMASTER product data sheet DS_CH_D8PLUS_SK_030-76U_500kg_4m_1f-400V-50Hz_DC.pdf rev 1.1 (18.10.2024) §2.2: 'Weight (without chain): approx. 20 kg' incl. suspension plate, hook tackle, direct control — https://chainmaster.de/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DS_CH_D8PLUS_SK_030-76U_500kg_4m_1f-400V-50Hz_DC.pdf
rigging.chain_kg_per_m_source: same data sheet §2.2: 'Weight of the chain: approx. 0.59 kg/m' (P5.4 × 15 mm, EN 818-7)
rigging.chain_carried_why: ESTIMATE: a hoist carries its whole chain (in the bag) whatever the drop; 12 m assumed until the rental house's hoists are known

drop.why: the SHORTEST drop the hoist allows: the hoist hangs straight from the bridle apex and is run up to its top at trim, so what swings under the apex is only the hoist itself

stack_m.basis: ESTIMATE (a 3.25 t bow shackle's inside length is ~60 mm)

stack_m.what: hoist, suspension plate hole to hook bottom at the shortest chain
stack_m.basis: CHAINMASTER SK030/76U dimension sheet (same PDF, §3.1/§3.2): suspension plate 97 + body 192 + chain exit 28 + hook tackle 227 mm — summed from the drawing (the maker states no single headroom figure)

stack_m.what: round sling, basket hitch over both top chords, on the hook

stack_m.basis: so the hoist never runs onto its upper limit at trim

bridle.what: each pick a two-leg bridle (a V) from the TWO girders of the bridge, apex over the line, the hoist under the apex — not one vertical chain: the V fixes the pick across the bridge (z)
bridle.attach: a girder beam clamp on the INNER edge of each girder's bottom flange (the girders' inner faces are 1.5 m apart: hall.json cranes girders_dz ±1.1, girder_w 0.7), a shackle, a steel leg to the apex
bridle.clamp_drop_basis: ESTIMATE: girder clamp jaw + shackle under the flange
bridle.max_included_why: the entertainment-rigging limit on a two-leg bridle (at 120° each leg carries the whole load; beyond, more than it): H. Donovan, Entertainment Rigging (2002), bridle tension tables — the high pick is designed AT it, the others far inside
bridle.hardware_basis: ESTIMATE: two girder clamps, two steels, shackles and ring per pick

rigging.safety: a secondary safety steel at every pick from the top chords to its OWN clamp on the back girder, independent of bridle and hoist (DGUV Vorschrift 17/18, BGV C1 practice: a secondary suspension for every load over people)

tieoffs.what: house-left end to the nave column at x −11.6 (inner face) on grid line z 6.0, at the end's own height — a 2 t LC ratchet strap (EN 12195-2) or a 6 mm steel with a turnbuckle

house-right end down to the nave column at x +11.6 on grid line z 6.0, at 4.6 m — UNDER the crane cab (audit A-02, 2026-10-05: at 5.5 m the strap ran through the cab; at 4.6 m it passes 0.23 m under the cab's 5.85 m bottom) and well under the crane runway beam (6.56–7.46 m on the column line); same strap or steel

rigging.tieoffs_why: the V bridles hold the line across the bridge; ALONG the line (x) each V still swings from its leg tops, and slings on a sloped chord want to creep downhill. Two opposed tie-offs, tensioned against each other (hand-tight, ~50 daN, ESTIMATE), hold it along x; each sling is choked against a node (a vertical brace) so it cannot slide down the slope (Prolyte user manual: loads applied at the nodes).
rigging.truss_kg_per_m_source: Prolyte H30V standard lengths table: H30V-L300 3.00 m 18.90 kg (https://www.prolyte.com/products/aluminium-truss/square-truss/h30v-l100-square-30-length-100-cm, read 2026-09-29) → 6.3 kg/m
rigging.extras_basis: clamps, safety bonds and the cable loom along the line: +10 % of the lamps — ESTIMATE
rigging.crane: the nave's entry-end bridge crane, rolled along its runway to park over the DJ (bridge centre line z 4.8, girder bottom 8.15 m — ESTIMATED; rail 7.6 m, range 6.6–8.4)
rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load, a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; bridle, tie-offs and safety steels to a rigger's plan with point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer; load cells on the three hoists at trim (a 3-point line is statically indeterminate: the middle pick's share moves with the chains' lengths). This file draws it; they approve it.

load.truss_basis: Prolyte H30V standard lengths table: H30V-L300 3.00 m 18.90 kg (https://www.prolyte.com/products/aluminium-truss/square-truss/h30v-l100-square-30-length-100-cm, read 2026-09-29) → 6.3 kg/m
load.extras_basis: clamps, safety bonds and the cable loom along the line: +10 % of the lamps — ESTIMATE
load.method: a continuous beam on three supports (flexibility method, versions.mjs threePointReactions), the lamps as point loads at their places, the truss as a uniform load; the hoist (datasheet 20 kg), its chain (0.59 kg/m × the chain carried) and the bridle hardware load the bridge on top (picks[].on_bridge_kg); leg tension = on-bridge load / (2 cos(half the included angle)). ESTIMATE, static, before any dynamic factor.
load.note: a 3-point line is statically indeterminate: this split holds for three hoists at one trim; the middle pick's share moves with the chains' lengths — load cells at trim. rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

clearance.note: the line hangs in the bridge's plane (z 4.8), behind the crowd barrier: no audience stands under it; the low end is over the back of house-left

motion.min_move_why: the owner's rule (2026-09-29): moving heads on a chain-hung line must not swing it — no full-range pan/tilt faster than 4 s, i.e. a cue that moves a head on the line fades in 4 s or more
motion.resonance_why: no periodic pan/tilt effect whose period lies within ±25 % of any natural period of the hang (method written down here, unvalidated: a common resonance-avoidance margin — machine foundations are kept ±20 % away; we take 25 %). Periods: T = 2π√(L/g), L the pendulum length (versions.mjs craneCut)

par.angleNote: the UP-PL5403's standard 15 deg lens (source D); candela scaled from the equivalent's 25 deg figure

lasercube.class: LaserCube Ultra MK2 — 10 W RGB laser projector, class 4 (the owner's own)
lasercube.angleNote: drawn as the narrowest cone di.iiii renders until the laser previs draws the streamed shapes; a real laser beam is millimetres wide and scanned into shapes
lasercube.intensityNote: no candela for a laser; never one of the real lamps (budget), so this is only the entity's value
lasercube.laserNote: drawn as a line source (laserLine.js): flux per diode from the manifest (variant_in_use, Guide v1.2), 4 mm, 1 mrad; never a three.js lamp (a 1 mrad SpotLight lights a sub-pixel dot)

groups.note: THE X: 3 PL5403 hung under each end (u ±4, ±4.5, ±5), all focused on one point 1 m over the DJ's head (x 0, 4.0 m, in the bridge's plane): the low left three rise into it, the high right three fall into it, and they cross — MOXIR's X over the DJ. Hung, not standing: standing on a 15° chord their beams would run through the truss. Fixed focus.
4 PL5403 standing on the cut (u ±2, ±3.5), grazing the underside of the bridge's audience-side girder outward in deep red — the crane drawn as a frame (kept from the flat line). Fixed focus.

THE CURTAIN: 7 PL5403 hung under the middle 6 m of the cut (u 0, ±1, ±2, ±3 — a metre apart), straight down, white only: in haze a sheet of white whose top edge IS the slope (the Minimal's cob-cut-curtain, with PARs: known-full has no COB200). Fixed focus — the same aim in every look.

one uplight on the inner face of each nave column around the dance floor and the stage (the 8 pairs z 6-48) — the back faces went to the vista and the forest: depth reads better than more brightness here.

3 PL5403 at the press's foot, on the backdrop line's clamp points (x 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 — 0.55/1.65/2.75 fell between them, so no look ever reached them: RIG_BUILD §19.4). The press rises out of the dark in the blade and the red room.
THE PRESS SCULPTED: 2 PL5403 low at the press's two sides (x 0.05 and 3.25, 0.35 m out), grazing its faces upward in cold white. Fixed focus.
THE VISTA: 8 PL5403 at the nave-side face of the four column pairs BEHIND the press (z -12, -24, -36, -48), straight up the column: the DJ against a 50 m tunnel of columns. Fixed focus.
THE FOREST: 4 PL5403 at the neighbour-span column rows (x ±36, z 18 and 30), straight up, deep red: the hall reads endless sideways. Fixed focus.

7 UP-B380F on the FLOOR of the backstage zone, 1.5 m behind the press (z -1.5, x -4.5 .. 4.5 at 1.5 m): behind the machinery, out of the crowd's reach and of the DJ's, rising into the roof frame so the press stands in silhouette in front of the shafts. Not behind the riser: the crane parked over the DJ (girders z 3.35-4.05 and 5.55-6.25) and the hung line stand in every beam from there.
10 beams at the column bases along the dance floor (z 24-48), 1.2 m off the inner face so the face's own PAR stands clear of them
THE LIGHTHOUSE: the 18th UP-B380F on the floor at the far back (x 0, z -48), straight up, white: seen from the floor it stands behind the DJ, 50 m deep.

6 LaserCube Ultra MK2 standing on the top chord of the cut at u ±1, ±3, ±5 — PROVISIONAL positions, to be decided with the owner in the room (2026-10-04). FIXED devices, clamped; nothing on them pans or tilts. Every beam up onto the solid roof deck beside the lantern over the house (laser-beside-lantern, audit A-03 2026-10-05: never into the lantern, a skylight), never into the audience plane (>= 3 m over any floor a person can stand on). Run OFF DMX: streamed over the wired network from di Raw. Class 4: needs a certified laser safety officer — OWNER SIGN-OFF, nothing here claims compliance.

effects.label: smoke / haze machine
effects.note: ONE UP-YZ31P on the floor beside a nave column: the only haze source of the kit (owner 2026-10-09). Run by hand at 100 % continuous in this version: an upper bound (duty cycle UNKNOWN). Never hung.

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.
budget.realNote: 2026-09-28 (DJ place): the press's own uplights stand 0.35 m from it, where a real lamp in the renderer blows the face out white; they are baked like the other PARs, and the 4 header spots (6.3 m up, over the DJ and the press) are the real lamps that light the backdrop.
budget.realLightsWhy: EVERY lamp is a real light (Emily 2026-10-01: 'i want 100% ident what we will have, you can optimize'): the room is the night as it will be, no picked few, no baked stand-ins. Measured on PONYO (RTX laptop, 1440x900): 40-52 fps; with shadows on the 12 lamps putting the most light in (shadowCasting.js shadowLampCap) 36-49 fps. A phone will not hold this: the 8-lamp budget is the fallback.

night.note: Darker than the base's readable night (ambient 0.8 -> 0.5, directional 0.35 -> 0.22): darkness is part of the design here (rule 1); the hall must still read in a render. Tuned by eye on the RTX 3080, 2026-09-28.

atmosphere.anisotropyWhy: HG g 0.74: lasers-exact.md §3.2 (own Mie computation, 0.3-1 um glycol/oil droplets, 455-638 nm: g 0.70-0.77), ASSUMPTION backed by computation

haze.source: UNVALIDATED estimate. Two-zone near-field/far-field model (Nicas 1996, AIHA J 57:542; AIHA 'Mathematical Models for Estimating Occupational Exposure', ch. 6), with first-order loss. Hall air 186,890 m3 (the scanned hall, rigBounce.js). Machine: Antari Z-1500 III EQUIVALENT, 150 ml/min at 100 %, continuous (upper bound). Droplets, persistence, drying 1.5 min, 6 air changes/h, near field 3 m hemisphere, air speed 0.1 m/s: ASSUMED (hazeField.js). Not a measurement; the transmissometer test owed.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).
photometry.airWhy: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

gs-one-shaft.title: Blackout + one shaft
gs-one-shaft.intent: Black. One thin white shaft stands straight up from behind the press into the roof, the DJ a silhouette cut out of it. Nothing else.

gs-columns-below.title: Columns from below
gs-columns-below.intent: The eight column faces glow cold white from their feet and fade to black before the roof; a low white beam at the foot of each far column. The floor is dark, the structure stands up out of it.

gs-haze-wall.title: Haze wall
gs-haze-wall.intent: Haze rolls from behind the DJ; all seven booth beams stand straight up in a row, a wall of light in the haze behind the silhouette; the rest is dark. EFFECT: hazers on (hazer-back, hazer-hall) — NOT SIMULATED.

gs-roof-reveal.title: Roof reveal
gs-roof-reveal.intent: The space-frame roof appears in pieces: the beams behind the press fan open into the trusswork, then the column beams stand up beside them; a dim white graze along the crane bridge above. Still, no sweep.

gs-slow-fan.title: Slow fan
gs-slow-fan.intent: The column beams lean slowly in across the nave, the wall beams lean slowly out toward the side walls, the booth beams open into a wide fan up into the roof. The move is the slow crossfade in from the reveal (6 s); nothing flashes.

gs-cross-beams.title: Cross beams
gs-cross-beams.intent: Beams from both walls lean in and cross high over the dance floor, above head height, like a lattice in the haze. The booth beams stay upright and dim behind.

gs-red-room.title: Red room
gs-red-room.intent: Deep red only and low: the columns and the press glow red from their feet, a dim red graze on the crane bridge, the booth beams stand still and dim. The DJ is a dark shape against the red press. The roof stays black.

gs-white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
gs-white-cathedral.intent: The whole nave in cold white: every column beam straight up in mirrored pairs, the wall beams up the walls, the crane bridge grazed white from the cut above, a narrow fan behind the DJ, who stands as a silhouette against the lit press.

gs-laser-roof.title: Laser into the roof
gs-laser-roof.intent: OPTIONAL, NOT IN THE LOOP. In the dark, red laser lines from the top of the cut into the roof frame, one dim red shaft behind the DJ. Needs a certified laser safety officer before it is ever switched on. LASER: off by default; requiresLaserSignOff: written at level 0, the laser stays dark until a human raises it after a certified laser safety officer signs off (Class 4, owed).

k-doors.title: Doors
k-doors.intent: Before the first act: haze up, the nave columns barely glowing amber from their feet, the press a dim silhouette. Enough to find your way, nothing that performs.

k-the-x.title: The X
k-the-x.intent: The X of PARs on the cut lights the DJ from above while the column beams cross the nave in an X high over the floor — the rig drawing its own sign.

k-tunnel.title: Tunnel
k-tunnel.intent: The ten column beams lean hard in from both walls and meet in a pointed arch high over the dance floor: a tunnel of white in the haze, the crowd underneath it.

k-green-core.title: Green core
k-green-core.intent: MOXIR's green, once: every nave column glows green from its foot and the press goes green behind the DJ, while a narrow white fan stands up behind the booth. The only colour in the night that is the brand's.

k-amber-dust.title: Amber dust
k-amber-dust.intent: The teaser's warm sodium light: amber up the columns and under the crane bridge, low, like dust in a factory afternoon. No beams. A breath between the white sections.

k-lights-up.title: Lights up
k-lights-up.intent: The end of the night: every column and the crane bridge in warm white at full, all beams off. Clean-out light, not a show look.

k-blade.title: The blade
k-blade.intent: The curtain at full white under the cut: in haze a sheet of cold white whose top edge is the cut's 15° slope; the four bridge PARs red at 60 % draw the crane as a frame. Nothing else.

k-hit.title: The hit
k-hit.intent: From black: the curtain and the six X PARs at full white together. No strobe channel (rates are untested on the PL5403) — the hit is the cue's own 0 s cut in and out.

k-one-shaft.title: One shaft on the DJ
k-one-shaft.intent: Black. The centre curtain PAR alone, full white, straight down on the DJ: one hard shaft from the cut, the DJ in it. Nothing else.

k-cathedral-x.title: White cathedral + the X
k-cathedral-x.intent: White cathedral with the X of PARs on the cut drawn over the DJ.

k-fan-hit.title: Fan hit
k-fan-hit.intent: From black, the seven booth beams open in a narrow white fan straight up behind the DJ. No sparks (no chart); the cue cuts in at 0 s.

k-monolith.title: Monolith
k-monolith.intent: The press stands up out of the dark: five PARs graze its faces from its foot in cold white, and far behind it, 50 m deep, one narrow white shaft, the lighthouse. Nothing else. The opening and rest look.

k-vista.title: Vista
k-vista.intent: The DJ against a 50 m tunnel: the eight PARs up the columns behind the press in cold white, near pair to far pair, the lighthouse at the end of them, and the centre booth beam backlighting the DJ at 30 %.

k-lightbox.title: Light box
k-lightbox.intent: The ten column-base beams lean inward at the policy's limit and light the roof lantern from inside as ten parallel planes; the crowd columns glow red at 20 %. The crowd stands under a glowing box; the gap over the DJ stays dark.

k-forest.title: Forest
k-forest.intent: Deep red only: the crowd columns and the neighbour-span columns at 60 %, the bridge red. The hall reads endless sideways. Everything else is dark.

k-crown.title: Crown
k-crown.intent: The climax, all white: the ten column beams lean into the lantern, the seven booth beams open in a fan behind the DJ, the vista and the lighthouse at full, the press lit. Nothing aims over the crowd.

movingFixtures.owner: 2026-09-30: "nothing moving on the air truss … no moving heads for now. All moving heads on the ground … statics go to the air truss, moving heads all safe on the ground, and 2 lasers."
movingFixtures.rule: no fixture that pans, tilts, rotates or zooms by motor is mounted above 0.6 m (its mounting face); no ground mover's beam passes through the dance zone below 2.5 m in any look; the six LaserCubes are fixed, and every laser beam stays >= 3 m over any floor a person can stand on.

lasers.signoff: Class 4: 6 LaserCube Ultra MK2 at 10 W each — a certified laser safety officer must approve the positions and the show (owner sign-off, owed); nothing in this file claims compliance.
lasers.aim: laser-beside-lantern: each beam onto the solid roof deck beside the lantern, never into the lantern (a skylight) — audit A-03, 2026-10-05; a laser safety officer still has to assess the reflections off the roof steel and the deck
lasers.drive: the six cubes are NOT on the desk: every look and cue leaves them dark (0). They are driven live from di Raw over the wired network (owner 2026-10-04); the room draws their beams as fixed cones only until the laser previs draws the streamed shapes — the sim does not show the lasers' show (audit A-04)

dmx.owner: 2026-10-01: hazers and smoke run by hand, off DMX; 2026-10-04: the 6 LaserCube Ultra MK2 run off DMX, streamed from di Raw over the wired network

opening.note: the first screen of the crane rig: 14 m out on the dance floor, on the centre line, eye height, looking up to 5.2 m so the crane bridge and the line hung under it frame the DJ, the press glowing behind (tuned by looking, 2026-09-28 night: at 20 m / 4.6 m the bridge read small over an empty floor)
